title: Chapter 21: The Theory of Spiritual Roots
paragraphs: The Grand Medical Palace had conducted extensive research on the relationship between Spiritual Roots and cultivation speed, culminating in the medical classicTreatise on Spiritual Roots.
The research revealed a direct proportionality between Spiritual Root attribute points and cultivation speed.

Every cultivator born under normal circumstances, endowed with ample innate vital energy, possesses 100 Spiritual Root attribute points. These points are then distributed across the Five Elements Attributes—Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, and Earth—forming each cultivator's unique Spiritual Root.
The distribution of attribute points among the Five Elements determines the efficiency of cultivation techniques.

For instance, a prodigy with extraordinary luck might allocate all 100 points to the Wood Element Spiritual Root, achieving the legendary Perfect Wood Heavenly Spiritual Root. This would double their cultivation speed for Wood Attribute techniques compared to ordinary cultivators. A technique that normally takes 100 years to master would require only 50 years.
Chen Mobai's current Spiritual Root attributes are: Metal 23, Wood 27, Water 30, Fire 17, Earth 10.

Taking his highest Water Attribute Spiritual Root as an example, if he were to cultivate the Blackwater Art and apply the formula from theTreatise on Spiritual Roots, his efficiency in refining Spiritual Energy would be only 1.3 times that of an average cultivator.

Of course, the actual cultivation efficiency depended on factors like the concentration of Spiritual Energy, the cultivator's mindset, and the presence of Cultivation Assistants, making it impossible to generalize.
Under ideal conditions, given Chen Mobai's natural talent, breaking through to the Sixth Layer of Qi Refinement using the Five Elements Art would take at least half a year.

The Water Abode, however, was a Second-Tier Mid-Grade Spiritual Land, with Spiritual Energy concentrations five to six times higher than a First-Tier High-Grade Spiritual Land. Cultivating here was like riding a rocket compared to studying at school or home.

Even so, due to the limitations of his Spiritual Root, Chen Mobai had previously calculated that he would still need a hundred days—nearly until the eve of the college entrance exams—to barely reach the Sixth Layer of Qi Refinement.
This was before he watched the video of Venerable Qingping's lecture.

As befitting a Nascent Soul Venerable, even when explaining the most basic Five Elements Art, Venerable Qingping delivered profound insights. Despite the lengthy, seemingly irrelevant preamble, when he finally delved into the core techniques, Chen Mobai experienced a sudden, enlightening awakening.
He learned that when Spiritual Power circulated through this meridian, rotating it counterclockwise seven times within the Apertures would effortlessly clear any blockages.

When drawing Spiritual Energy through the three Apertures of the mouth and nose, it was crucial to repeatedly circulate it through the Twelve-Story Tower in the throat. This allowed the twelve segments to filter out impurities from the external Spiritual Energy, preventing them from entering the body's meridians. Upon completing the practice, this stale breath would be spat out from the throat.
Conversely, when refined Spiritual Energy converged into the Sea of Qi in the dantian, it should be channeled in thin, continuous streams with a rightward spiral.

Since rightward spirals move clockwise—clockwise being synonymous with advancement—this technique aids in condensing Spiritual Power. Foundation Establishment, the process of transforming Spiritual Power into a liquid state, can be accelerated by incorporating this step, thereby increasing the success rate of future Foundation Establishment by ten percent.

Conversely, leftward spirals represent reversal and dispersion. When circulating Spiritual Power through particularly blocked or narrow meridians, forcing it through would be counterproductive. Instead, the Spiritual Power should be dispersed into a thin, pliable Qi, allowing it to advance slowly and gently.

After completing his cultivation session, Chen Mobai reviewed the videos explaining the first and second layers of the Five Elements Art in the Qi Refinement stage. Only then did he realize how superficial his previous understanding of this fundamental cultivation technique had been.
As dawn approached, he reluctantly turned off his phone, his heart heavy with reluctance.
During his cultivation session that night, Chen Mobai had used the offline download feature to save all twenty-eight videos of Venerable Qingping's lectures on the Five Elements Art to his phone.
This offline download feature was a privilege reserved for Cultivation Assistant users of Tier 3 and above. As a Tier 5 user, Chen Mobai naturally had access to it.
To be cautious, he turned off his phone's cellular data before going to class that morning to avoid any unwanted contact from the Cultivation Assistant's operators.
"Did you hear? Yan Bingxuan dropped out."
That morning, before the teacher arrived, Lu Hongsheng, Chen Mobai's deskmate, leaned in conspiratorially. Unable to contain the explosive news, he blurted it out directly.
"Huh? Why? The college entrance exams are right around the corner. Did she drop out because she couldn't handle losing to Song Zheng?"
"Most likely. She's always been aloof and proud. Losing face like that must have been too much to bear, so she just quit."
"That doesn't make sense. She's lost before."
"Maybe she's using dropping out as an excuse to secretly work harder at home."
The two beautiful girls at the table in front leaned closer, and the students at the table behind, not wanting to miss out, quickly formed a gossip circle centered around Chen Mobai and Lu Hongsheng.
Chen Mobai could only roll his eyes. Normally, he would have joined in, but now that it was his senior year—a crucial time to work hard—he had no time for idle gossip.
He was determined to make a name for himself, to soar to great heights...
Just then, Yan Bingxuan walked in, and the gossip circle instantly fell silent.

Her icy gaze swept across the room, and Chen Mobai gestured his innocence, indicating he hadn't participated in the discussion. But Great Beauty Yan merely glanced at him coldly for two seconds before returning to her seat, silently packing her things, slinging her blue backpack over her shoulder, and leaving the classroom.
The classroom remained silent for about ten seconds before erupting into excited chatter and whispered conversations.
Even the students who had doubted Lu Hongsheng's information now cast astonished glances their way, causing Chen Mobai's deskmate to puff out his chest with pride.
Chen Mobai stood up, his chair scraping against the floor.
"Where are you going? Class is about to start," Lu Hongsheng asked, puzzled.

"I forgot my textbook. I'm going to borrow one from the library," Chen Mobai replied, quickly excusing himself to avoid the increasingly absurd gossip and speculation that was about to erupt. The students behind him had already concocted an elaborate love-hate drama between the two geniuses, Song Zheng and Yan Bingxuan, worthy of a twenty-episode TV series.
He couldn't bear to listen any longer.
Since he was already planning to borrow theFive Elements Arttextbook from the library, he seized the opportunity to slip away.

Immortal Sect Fifth High School boasted a small library with around three thousand books. It housed commonly used biographies, histories, volumes on Danxia City's customs and culture, and self-study manuals covering minor spells, cultivation techniques, medicinal pills, artifacts, array formations, and more.

Although the highest-grade items were only First-Tier High-Grade, the library offered comprehensive foundational knowledge across various fields. With diligent study and comprehension of all its contents, one could easily pass the certification exams for First-Tier Array Formation Master, Pill Refiner, or Artifact Appraiser.
Unfortunately, the library remained largely deserted.
What era is this? Who still reads paper books?
Only those who forgot their textbooks would come here to borrow books for half a day using their student cards, returning them after school.

If Chen Mobai hadn't been reluctant to spend 10 Points to download the electronic version of theFive Elements Artfrom the Immortal Sect National Electronic Library, he wouldn't have bothered borrowing a physical copy from this library.

Yesterday, he had benefited greatly from Venerable Qingping's lecture, but when reviewing the earlier material, he found it had already become somewhat hazy. He felt it necessary to cross-reference the originalFive Elements Arttextbook with the lecture videos to reinforce his comprehension.
"One copy of theFive Elements Art, borrowed with your student card, free for one month."
The librarian, a teacher wearing round-framed glasses, skillfully took Chen Mobai's student card and swiped it.
Just as Chen Mobai was thanking her and turning to leave, someone suddenly walked through the library's entrance.
